summary: Cheap, founder-sellable, low-CAC motion fits a solo founder, but the ROI pitch (GB saved) only bites for MSSPs on per-GB SIEMs like Sentinel; Wazuh, Graylog Open and Elastic self-hosted don't bill ingest, and Cribl is free to 1TB/day. A flat $249 for 50 tenants caps expansion and leaves churn-prone, copyable content as the whole subscription.

objections.objection: The dollar ROI behind the price applies to a minority of the named targets. Self-hosted Wazuh, Graylog Open and Elastic have no ingest fee; Wazuh Cloud is priced by agents and retention ($571/month for up to 100 agents), Huntress and Blumira are flat. Only Sentinel-style per-GB SIEMs turn 'GB saved' into cash, so the 'log diet' wedge mostly yields disk savings, not a budget line.

The rationale says pipeline tools are priced for enterprises, but Cribl Stream's Free tier processes up to 1TB/day with unlimited pipelines, far above any 10-150-client SMB MSSP's Windows volume. The real price anchor is free (Cribl Free plus community Sysmon configs plus built-in Sysmon), so $249/month must be justified by maintenance and support alone.

Flat $249/month for up to 50 tenants (~$5/tenant) has no expansion path: revenue doesn't grow as the MSSP adds clients, and MSPs who resell per client get no per-client SKU to mark up. At ~$3k ACV, $300k ARR needs ~100 paying MSSPs from a niche of small security-led MSPs. Per-client comparables are far higher (ADAudit Plus $495-595/yr per 2 servers; Wazuh Cloud $571/month).

Churn risk is structural: once configs are deployed via GPO/RMM, a customer can cancel and keep running them; Sysmon/audit-policy schemas change rarely, so 'monthly maintenance' may not be felt as monthly value. Subscription retention depends on recurring deliverables (new detections, per-client reports) not yet defined.

First-ten plan leans on r/msp and vendor-neutral communities plus 'a few contacts'; vendor self-promotion is policed there, and the success signal (3 paid pilots and 10 pricing requests in 2 weeks) is optimistic. Pilot price ($500) and tuning price ($2,500) are inconsistent, muddying the paid-pilot test.
Liability for dropped events could force contract terms (indemnity caps, coverage SLAs) that a $249 subscription can't carry, lengthening procurement with MSSPs that have their own client contracts.

strongest_point: Low price, open-source inbound and founder-led tuning give revenue from month one with near-zero CAC, in the founder's own specialty, sold through MSPs who already deploy via RMM.
what_would_change_my_mind: Data showing at least 40% of target MSSPs pay per-GB ingest (e.g. Sentinel, Graylog Security)
3 pilots converting to subscriptions at a per-client price (e.g. $5-15/client/month) with 6-month retention
An RMM or SIEM vendor willing to OEM or marketplace-list the packs
